contracts.scope: Bounded imported single-parameter generic field-versus-nil predicate inlining. No source edits, builds, or tests were performed for this audit.

contracts.observation: A generic GetField can invoke __index. The callback can inspect its caller source or function using debug.getinfo(2), and inlining removes the provider frame.
contracts.archivedTrialCorrection: The fact producer was changed to require callee-scoped @relax("frames", "error-site"). Unrelaxed providers must retain their call.

contracts.observation: An __index callback can raise at a chosen caller level. Removing its provider frame changes source attribution even when the field operation itself is retained.
contracts.archivedTrialCorrection: Require explicit error-site relaxation in addition to frames; neither permission implies the other.

contracts.observation: A simple-looking provider.present(...) can be a checker-qualified namespace projection rather than a local imported binding. Its normal lowering emits Require before GetField. Skipping callee evaluation can suppress module initialization.
contracts.archivedTrialCorrection: Reject qualifiedModule/compilerModule/namespacePath callees and arguments. Admit only stable lexical imported bindings in this trial.

contracts.observation: The runtime documents function IDs as the stable callable identity and replacement bodies as visible on each next call. vm.hotPatch forwards one module image to hotpatch::apply. Same-signature, same-capture provider body edits are accepted unless linked native code prevents replacement; no inline dependency registry or importer-version guard is checked.
contracts.failure: After present(value) changes from value.tag ~= nil to value.other ~= nil, an old inlined importer still reads tag while a real call by ID reads other.

contracts.observation: Source watch revalidates loaded roots but compiles patch images only for changed paths. Inferred callable facts are deliberately excluded from runtime ABI comparisons, so a changed predicate fact alone does not force a restart or produce an importer patch.
contracts.failure: A provider-only file event can patch the provider while unchanged importer source keeps running its old inlined bytecode.

contracts.observation: When callable facts are published, fresh or cached whole-image emission can invalidate importers correctly: interface images preserve callGuarantees, interfaceOf hashes the encoded full interface, and fragment replay checks dependency digests. The rejected trial published inlinePredicate through that existing path.
contracts.boundary: These build-time checks produce correct new images. They do not modify already-running importer bodies or constrain raw patch acceptance.

whyTheTwoRelaxationsAreInsufficient: frames permits removing the provider activation; error-site permits changed error attribution.
Neither permission authorizes a different field predicate or stale return values after an otherwise accepted provider body patch.
Neither permission authorizes removing implicit module initialization; load-order is a separate guarantee.
Correct cached image rebuilding does not establish correctness of a running image after a provider-only patch.

futurePrerequisites.requirement: Choose and enforce an explicit live-body dependency policy before enabling cross-module bytecode inlining.
soundOptions: Keep calls in all reloadable images, with enforceable runtime policy identifying immutable images/providers.
Guard the inlined body against provider generation or body identity and fall back to the ordinary call after a change.
Record inline dependencies and require recompilation/publication of affected importers as part of a coordinated patch transaction.
Mark providers whose bodies were inlined as nonpatchable and reject their replacement at runtime.

futurePrerequisites.requirement: Cover both compiler-managed watch and direct vm.hotPatch. Disabling only watch inlining leaves direct raw patch behavior unresolved.
Add regressions for provider-only raw body replacement, provider-only watch events, relaxation removal, frame-sensitive __index, error attribution, and qualified namespace initialization.
If runtime dependency metadata or guards are added, preserve them through worker code recipes, snapshots, and hotpatch replay.
Retain exact callable identity, mutation safeguards, closed fact validation, generic GetField semantics, and fresh/cached image equivalence.
After semantic acceptance, measure the representative root emit using distinct matching compiler images and the standing paired cycle margin. A hotspot share is not a measured speedup.

relax-default.excerpt:
A guarantee is a property of a running program that a reader could notice, and
Nupp keeps every one of them by default. `@relax` says a function may give one
up, which is what lets a rewrite that would otherwise change observable behavior
apply there.

relax-callee.excerpt:
That says two things about `dispatch`: a traceback through it need not show the
frames it would have shown, and an error raised inside it need not report the
position it would have reported. Nothing else about it changes.

frames-permission.excerpt: | `frames` | a traceback shows the frames the source describes | inlining a call away |

error-site-permission.excerpt: | `error-site` | an error reports the position that raised it | hoisting a check or a chain out of a loop |

load-order-permission.excerpt: | `load-order` | modules initialize in the order the requires run | hoisting an import, or binding a callee statically |
